rounds.proof_sketch: With block_size=256, there are 8 warps per block (warp_id 0-7). All warps execute identical operations: 16 loop iterations, constant-time fabsf() and shuffle operations, coalesced memory access. Thread execution time is independent of input values. The removed sync creates a race between warp_sums writes (warps 1-7) and reads (warp 0), but this timing cannot be influenced by tensor values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes a __syncthreads() creating a theoretical race condition, but this race is timing-dependent, not value-dependent. All threads execute identical code paths with identical operation counts regardless of input values. Float operations (fabsf, addition) and shuffle instructions have constant latency independent of operand magnitude. The warp scheduler naturally keeps warps synchronized given the uniform workload distribution. 112 differential tests passing (including structured ramps, sparse, boundary, and large magnitude tests) empirically confirms that the race cannot be triggered through value manipulation on the test hardware.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant cannot be killed through value manipulation alone. The race condition requires hardware-level timing variations that input values cannot control. The synchronization bug would require either different GPU hardware, kernel configuration changes (more warps, different block sizes), or runtime conditions outside the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of synchronization barriers, consider testing across multiple GPU architectures or using CUDA-MEMCHECK/compute-sanitizer race detection tools. Value-level testing alone cannot expose timing-dependent races where all threads execute uniform workloads. Consider adding static analysis rules that flag removed __syncthreads() between shared memory write and read patterns as semantically non-equivalent even when runtime tests pass.
